changesApplied.changeMade: Added backend sync after local write: calls metabob_impulse_store via CLI MCP with (impulse_id, project_id, impulse_data)
changesApplied.reason: Enforces vessel flow (opencode -> CLI MCP -> rpc-api -> SurrealDB) so impulses are instance-invariant. Instance A creates impulse -> Instance B can retrieve it from backend.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Non-breaking: backend sync is best-effort (wrapped in try-catch). Local storage still works if MCP client unavailable. Adds ~50ms latency for backend call.
changesApplied.vesselFlowEnforcement: YES - calls CLI MCP tool metabob_impulse_store instead of direct backend access

changesApplied.changeMade: Added backend sync after local write: calls metabob_activity_save via CLI MCP with (activity_id, project_id, activity_data)
changesApplied.reason: Enforces vessel flow for activity persistence. Activities are now stored in backend (SurrealDB) for cross-instance access, not just local filesystem.
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Non-breaking: backend sync is best-effort. Tool availability is checked before call (metabob_activity_save may not be deployed yet). Local storage unaffected.
changesApplied.vesselFlowEnforcement: YES - calls CLI MCP tool metabob_activity_save, checks tool existence before call

changesApplied.changeMade: Added backend fallback for read operations: if local Storage.read fails, calls metabob_activity_load via CLI MCP with (activity_id, project_id)
changesApplied.reason: Enables cross-instance retrieval. Instance B can now load activities created by Instance A even if not in local cache. Implements dual-layer: local (cache) + backend (source of truth).
changesApplied.impactAnalysis: Non-breaking: local read is still tried first (fast path). Backend fallback only on local failure. Successfully loaded backend activities are cached locally for future access.
changesApplied.vesselFlowEnforcement: YES - calls CLI MCP tool metabob_activity_load as fallback, respects vessel boundaries

annotations.reason: Dual-write pattern: local write for fast access + backend sync for cross-instance invariance. Backend sync is best-effort (non-critical failure) to maintain backward compatibility.
annotations.designDecision: Vessel flow enforcement: opencode must call CLI MCP tools, not rpc-api directly. This maintains architectural boundaries and enables gateway-level concerns (auth, rate limiting, logging).

annotations.reason: Same dual-write pattern as impulses. Checks tool availability before call since metabob_activity_save may not be deployed yet (graceful degradation).
annotations.designDecision: Tool availability check prevents runtime errors during rollout. Once CLI tools deployed, backend sync activates automatically.

annotations.reason: Backend fallback enables cross-instance access. Local-first strategy (try cache first) maintains performance while backend provides source of truth.
annotations.designDecision: Cache locally after backend load to reduce future backend calls. This hybrid approach balances performance (local cache) with consistency (backend fallback).

Dual-storage pattern: local (cache) + backend (source of truth)
performanceRequirements: Backend sync adds <100ms latency (acceptable for write operations)
Backend fallback only on local miss (rare case after warm-up)
